types.name: LogRingBuffer
types.doc:
Ring buffer retained for post-crash log recovery. Producers are every
thread in the process, so the slot write and the index advance have to be
one atomic step — a mutex, not a pair of atomics.

members.name: GetAll
members.doc:
Best-effort snapshot. The crash handler runs on the faulting thread,
which may itself hold m_mutex, so a failed lock reads on anyway rather
than deadlocking and losing the dump entirely.

types.name: LogRecord
types.doc:
One line of log output, pre-formatted and ready for a sink.
The redirector holds a mutex during fan-out, so a single
Serialize() call never interleaves lines across sinks.

members.name: message
members.doc: already formatted (printf result)

members.name: Serialize
members.doc:
Called from the Logger for every MOWO_LOG_* call that survives
its category's verbosity gate. Implementations are free to
re-filter (a noisy sink might raise its own threshold).

members.name: Flush
members.doc:
Optional: flush buffered output. Called by the redirector on
shutdown and from FOutputDeviceRedirector::Flush().

members.name: GetName
members.doc: Human-readable name for diagnostics.

members.name: AddOutputDevice
members.doc:
Register a sink. Caller retains ownership — the redirector never
deletes the device; cleanup after RemoveOutputDevice() is the
caller's job.

members.name: RemoveOutputDevice
members.doc:
Detach a previously-added sink. Safe to call from inside
Serialize() — the broadcast iterates a snapshot of the list.

members.name: Serialize
members.doc:
Fan out one record to every registered sink. Thread-safe;
sinks themselves are responsible for internal locking.

members.name: Flush
members.doc: Flush every registered sink (before shutdown, before a crash dump upload).

members.name: SetMinLevel
members.doc: Sinks see records at or above this level only. Default Trace.

types.name: FLogCategory
types.doc:
A named log category with its own runtime threshold, the UE5 model. Messages
below the threshold cost one relaxed atomic load and are dropped before the
arguments are formatted.

Storage discipline matters: declare with the owning module's export macro in
a header and define in exactly ONE .cpp. An inline static would hand every
DLL its own copy, and `log <category> <level>` would then reach whichever one
the console happened to resolve — the same trap that duplicated event type
ids across modules.

members.name: ParseLevel
members.signature: static bool ParseLevel(std::string_view text, LogLevel& out)
members.doc:
Parses "trace"/"debug"/"info"/"warning"/"error"/"fatal" (case-insensitive,
"warn" accepted). False leaves `out` untouched.

members.name: RegisterConsoleCommand
members.doc:
Registers the `log` console command: `log` lists every category and its
level, `log <category> <level>` sets one, `log <category> reset` restores
the level it was declared with. Called once during engine init.

members.name: CrashFlush
members.doc:
The crash path's flush: the process may already be broken and another
thread may hold this sink's lock forever, so it must never block on
it and never allocate. Defaults to Flush for sinks that hold nothing.

members.name: ConsoleSink
members.signature: ConsoleSink(bool useColors = true, bool showLocation = true, bool allToStderr = false) : m_useColors(useColors && !allToStderr), m_showLocation(showLocation), m_allToStderr(allToStderr)
members.doc:
`allToStderr` keeps stdout for a protocol: the editor's --mcp-stdio
speaks JSON-RPC on it, one message per line, and a log line or a colour
escape in between is a corrupt message to the client.

types.name: FileSink
types.doc:
Lines land in a memory buffer and reach the disk from a flusher thread
every 200 ms, when the buffer fills, on any Error/Fatal line, on Flush,
and from the crash handler's pre-report hook — never with a syscall per
line. The old sink wrote std::endl per message, one flush each, which
was a measurable share of a Debug frame under the render-init spam. The
file is opened shared-read so the crash reporter's tail copy and a tail
tool still see it mid-session.

No thread that logs ever waits on the disk. The flusher opens the file,
swaps the buffer out under the lock and writes it with the lock released;
an Error line only wakes it. The lock used to be held across fwrite and
fflush, and on a disk taking seconds per write (a project on a busy HDD)
every logging thread — the render thread included — froze behind it: the
owner's 14 s and 19 s "submit" stalls were the render thread waiting to
append one line. A disk that takes nothing for long enough costs lines,
counted in the file, never a frame.

members.name: SetWriteStallForTest
members.doc:
Holds every disk write of every FileSink this long — a test's stand-in
for a disk that takes seconds per write.

members.name: CrashFlush
members.doc:
What the crash handler runs before it copies the log tail: best
effort, no allocation, and never a wait on a lock the crashing thread
itself may hold.

members.name: ResolveLogsDir
members.doc:
Where the file sink writes: <project>/Saved/Logs when a project is
open, else <state root>/<Product>/Saved/Logs (Launcher, headless
self-tests, packaged games with no writable project).

members.name: Initialize
members.doc:
Opens the console + file sinks and rotates old Mowo_*.log files out.
Release builds keep both sinks OFF and the threshold at Warning
unless -log is on the command line or the game's Config sets
logging.enabled=true (the bUseLoggingInShipping model).

members.signature: static void PruneOldLogs(const std::filesystem::path& logsDir, size_t keep)
members.doc: Deletes the oldest Mowo_*.log / mowo_*.log files beyond `keep`.
